subject: orthopaedics
title: Osteonecrosis and osteochondritis: high-yield orthopaedics for NEET-PG

steps.tx: **Osteonecrosis** is death of bone from interrupted blood supply. Bone dies, subchondral fracture follows, and the joint eventually collapses. The femoral head is the commonest site, followed by the scaphoid, talus and lunate. Early X-rays are often normal, so **MRI** is the investigation of choice for early disease.
steps.say: Osteonecrosis is death of bone from interrupted blood supply. Bone dies, subchondral fracture follows, and the joint eventually collapses. The femoral head is the commonest site, followed by the scaphoid, talus and lunate. Early X-rays are often normal, so MRI is the investigation of choice for early disease.

steps.tx: Major causes include **steroid use**, alcoholism, hip trauma or dislocation, sickle cell disease, Gaucher disease and caisson disease. A nephrotic patient on long steroids who limps and has restricted abduction and internal rotation should raise suspicion of femoral head necrosis. Pain often refers to the groin, buttock or knee.

steps.tx: The **Ficat and Arlet** system stages hip necrosis. Stage I has no radiographic change, stage II shows subchondral bone change without collapse, stage III shows subchondral fracture with collapse, and stage IV shows collapse with acetabular involvement. The **crescent sign** on lateral X-ray marks subchondral collapse and is a late sign.

steps.tx: Osteochondritis is ischaemic necrosis of an articular or apophyseal bone segment in adolescents, often after repetitive stress. Crushing types include **Kohler** (navicular), **Kienbock** (lunate), **Freiberg** (metatarsal head) and **Perthes** (femoral head). Traction types include **Osgood-Schlatter** (tibial tubercle) and **Sever** (calcaneal apophysis).
steps.say: Osteochondritis is ischaemic necrosis of an articular or apophyseal bone segment in adolescents, often after repetitive stress. Crushing types include Kohler, affecting the navicular, Kienbock, affecting the lunate, Freiberg, affecting the metatarsal head, and Perthes, affecting the femoral head. Traction types include Osgood-Schlatter, affecting the tibial tubercle, and Sever, affecting the calcaneal apophysis.

steps.tx: **Osgood-Schlatter disease** affects active boys aged 10 to 15, causing pain and swelling over the tibial tubercle. Radiographs are usually unremarkable, and treatment is rest with activity modification. Natural history is benign. **Sinding-Larsen-Johansson** disease affects the lower pole of the patella in a similar way.
